title: Russia Strikes Zaporizhstal Steel Plant for 4th Time in a Month
detail: Russian forces struck the Zaporizhstal Iron and Steel Works with two ballistic missiles on the morning of September 17, injuring one staff member who was pulled from rubble with shrapnel injuries and a concussion. Metinvest, the plant's owner and Ukraine's largest steel producer, said it was the fourth strike on the facility in a little over a month and that Russia has fired 17 ballistic missiles at Zaporizhstal since August. The plant had been shut down following the August 11 strike that killed 6-7 workers. Metinvest COO Oleksandr Myronenko called the repeated strikes 'systemic terror against Ukrainian industry and people,' aimed at preventing repairs and destroying Ukrainian industrial capacity.

title: Russian Strike on Korosten Industrial Park Kills 2, Injures 2
detail: Russian forces struck an industrial park in the Korosten district of Zhytomyr Oblast on the evening of September 17, killing two people and injuring two others who were hospitalized in moderate condition. Fires broke out in warehouse and production buildings; 56 firefighters and 17 fire appliances from the State Emergency Service, along with Ukrainian Red Cross rapid response volunteers, worked through the night to extinguish the blazes, which were out by the following morning. The head of the Zhytomyr Oblast Military Administration said 'a civilian business has once again come under enemy attack in Zhytomyr Oblast,' referencing a prior strike on the region's police headquarters in August. The strike came amid a wider overnight barrage that Ukrainian officials said killed 6 and injured 34 nationwide, including 93 strike drones (46 jet-powered) and Banderol and Dan-T cruise missiles, of which Ukrainian air defenses downed or jammed 69 drones and 3 missiles.

title: Ukraine Launches 350+ Drone Attack Toward Moscow Region
detail: Ukraine launched more than 350 drones toward the Moscow region overnight from September 17 into September 18, in one of the largest such attacks on the Russian capital in years, according to Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin, who said the barrage ran from roughly 8 p.m. on September 17 to 7 a.m. the next morning. Sobyanin said 64 drones were destroyed on approach to Moscow; Russian officials did not release information on damage caused by debris. The strike was part of Ukraine's ongoing long-range campaign against Russian military-industrial and infrastructure targets in response to continued Russian attacks on Ukrainian cities, including the same day's strikes on Zaporizhstal and Zhytomyr Oblast.
